support.title: Support Famous Cities | Help an Independent Travel Project Grow
support.description: Support Famous Cities — an independent city-guide project. Learn what donations fund and how to contribute via GoFundMe or Ko-fi.
support.heading: Support Famous Cities and Its Creator
support.html:
I’m raising support for myself as the independent creator behind Famous Cities, an independent website I built to explore notable cities through their landmarks, histories, cultures, architecture, and unique identities. I created this project because of my personal interest in cities, and I want to keep expanding it into a larger and more engaging experience. Working on Famous Cities has given me a stronger sense of purpose, lets me share one of my hobbies with others, and has become a passive way for me to make income through hotel widget commissions on the site.

This fundraiser is personal support for me as I continue building and maintaining Famous Cities. Donations can give me greater freedom to keep researching, writing, programming, maintaining affiliate programs, improving the design, and developing new website content. Most donations may be used at my discretion for general personal expenses, which helps me continue putting time and energy into this project. A smaller portion may go directly toward website-related costs such as hosting, programming resources, affiliate-program expenses, research, digital assets, IP address expenses, and affiliate program costs for TravelPayouts and Stay22.

Because this is an ongoing creative project, the need for support is ongoing as well. Predictable recurring donations would help me continue covering the personal and website expenses that come with keeping Famous Cities active and growing over time. At the same time, one-time donations are also sincerely appreciated and make a real difference.

This is a personal fundraiser supporting me as an independent creator. Donations are voluntary gifts and do not provide products, services, website ownership, investment rights, profit participation, or financial returns.

If you enjoy Famous Cities, appreciate independent creative projects, or simply want to support me and my work, please consider contributing. Every donation is appreciated, regardless of size, and sharing this fundraiser with people interested in cities, culture, history, architecture, or travel would also help tremendously. If the website grows enough and I have the means in the future, I hope to be in a position to give back generously to others as well. Thank you for supporting me and the continued growth of Famous Cities.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy & Affiliate Disclosure | Famous Cities
privacy.description: How Famous Cities handles your information, cookies and affiliate links.
privacy.heading: Privacy Policy & Affiliate Disclosure
privacy.html:
Last updated: October 2026

Who we are

Famous Cities is an independent travel guide to some of the world's most famous cities. If you have any questions about this page, email thekunsaw@gmail.com.

Affiliate disclosure

Some links on this site—for example to hotels, homes, flights and tours—are affiliate links. If you click one and make a booking, Famous Cities may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you. These partners do not pay to be mentioned in our city guides, and we only link to services we think travelers will find useful. Prices and availability are set by each partner and can change at any time.

Information we collect

You can read Famous Cities without creating an account or giving us any personal information. We only receive personal information, such as your name and email address, if you choose to email us.

Cookies and analytics

We may use a privacy-friendly analytics service to understand which pages and links are popular, such as page views, the country you are visiting from, your device type and which booking buttons are clicked. This information is used in aggregate to improve the site and is not used to identify you.

When you click an affiliate link, the partner website (for example Booking.com, Expedia or Viator) may place its own cookies in your browser so it can credit the booking to us. Those cookies are controlled by the partner and covered by its own privacy policy. Some outbound links may also be routed through affiliate networks such as Stay22 or Travelpayouts, which track the referral so the booking can be credited to this site.

This site also uses your browser's local storage to remember the city pages you have viewed and any travel dates you enter, so they are prefilled when you return. This information stays in your own browser, is never sent to us, and can be cleared by deleting your browser data.

Third-party content

Some pages include content from other services, such as embedded YouTube videos and links to social networks and Wikipedia. These services may collect information according to their own privacy policies when you interact with them.

Donations

If you choose to support Famous Cities with a donation, any payment is processed by the payment provider you use, and we do not store your card details.

Children

Famous Cities is a general travel guide and is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children.

Your choices

You can block or delete cookies in your browser settings at any time. If you have emailed us and want us to delete your message or contact details, just ask using the email address above.

Changes to this page

We may update this page from time to time. The date at the top shows when it was last changed.

dubai-3-day-budget.title: Is a 3-Day Dubai Trip Possible on a Budget? 2026 Cost Breakdown | Famous Cities
dubai-3-day-budget.description: Dubai on a budget is real: abra rides for AED 1, free beaches and fountains, metro over taxis. A 3-day itinerary with real 2026 costs at $60-90/day.
dubai-3-day-budget.heading: Is a 3-Day Dubai Trip Possible on a Budget? (2026 Cost Breakdown)
dubai-3-day-budget.html:
Short answer: yes. Dubai’s skyline screams luxury, but the city underneath it is full of world-class experiences that cost almost nothing — a one-dirham boat crossing, free beaches, free fountain shows, and some of the best cheap food in the Middle East. Here’s how to do 3 days on roughly $60–90 per day (excluding flights).

The real numbers

A budget bed in Deira or Bur Dubai runs AED 80–150/night ($22–41). A Nol metro card costs about AED 20–40 per day of riding. Eating where locals eat — shawarma, Pakistani and Indian cafeterias, Iranian kebab houses — runs AED 40–80 a day. Total: AED 200–300 ($55–80) per day, versus $400+ at the luxury end.

Day 1: Old Dubai — nearly free

Start in the Al Fahidi historical district (free), then cross Dubai Creek on a wooden abra — AED 1, still the best-value boat ride on earth. Wander the Gold and Spice Souks in Deira (free, and haggling is expected), then lunch at a Bur Dubai cafeteria for under AED 20.

Day 2: The icons — pick your splurge

The Dubai Mall’s aquarium viewing panel is free from the concourse. The Burj Khalifa fountain show runs every 30 minutes each evening — also free. Your one paid ticket: At the Top observation deck, from about AED 179 if you book an off-peak slot online in advance (walk-up peak prices are far higher). Alternative cheaper icon: Dubai Frame, around AED 50.

Day 3: Beach + desert

Kite Beach and JBR’s public beach are free all day. At sunset, either splurge on a desert safari (AED 100–150 with dinner) or take the free option: sunset views of Atlantis from The Pointe on the Palm monorail side, or from the Marina promenade.

Budget rules that actually work

Ride the metro, not taxis — the Red Line covers the airport, Dubai Mall, Marina and JBR. Eat in Deira and Bur Dubai, not the Marina. Book every ticket online in advance; gate prices are the tourist trap. And refill a water bottle at the mall — AED 10 bottles add up fast.

For everything else — maps, fun facts, ranked hotels and tour links — see the full guide below.

dubai-layover-guide.title: 10-Hour Dubai Layover: Burj Khalifa & Dubai Mall Plan (2026) | Famous Cities
dubai-layover-guide.description: A 10-hour Dubai layover is enough for the Burj Khalifa and Dubai Mall. The exact plan: metro times, visa rules, ticket booking, and the return-flight buffer.
dubai-layover-guide.heading: How to See the Burj Khalifa and Dubai Mall on a 10-Hour Layover
dubai-layover-guide.html:
Dubai International (DXB) is one of the busiest transit hubs on earth, and the city is built for exactly this. A 10-hour layover gives you roughly 5–6 usable hours — enough for the world’s tallest building and the world’s most-visited mall, comfortably.

First: can you leave the airport?

Many nationalities — including US, UK and EU passport holders — get a free 30-day visa on arrival. Others can arrange a 48- or 96-hour transit visa through Emirates or a hotel. Check your eligibility before you fly; rules change.

Flying Emirates? If your connection is forced to 8+ hours, ask about Dubai Connect — a free hotel, meals and visa that the airline sometimes includes.

Getting downtown

Take the Red Line metro straight from Terminal 1 or 3 to Burj Khalifa/Dubai Mall station: about 25 minutes and a few dirhams. A taxi takes 15–20 minutes and costs AED 50–70. Leave your bags in DXB’s left-luggage facility or travel with a cabin bag only.

The 6-hour plan

Hours 0–1: Immigration (usually fast), metro to Dubai Mall.

Hours 1–3: Burj Khalifa. Book your timed “At the Top” ticket weeks ahead — Level 124/125 slots sell out and walk-up prices are punishing. The observation deck visit takes about 90 minutes.

Hours 3–5: Dubai Mall. The giant aquarium viewing panel is free from the concourse, and the Souk Al Bahar across the bridge is the best quick lunch with a fountain view. If your layover lands in the evening, the fountain show runs every 30 minutes from 6pm.

Hours 5–6: Metro back to DXB. Be through security 2 hours before departure — Dubai’s gates can be a 20-minute walk away.

Layover mistakes to avoid

Don’t book the Burj Khalifa at the desk on the day — timed slots are cheaper and guaranteed online. Don’t underestimate terminal walking distances at DXB. And don’t try to squeeze in the desert or the Marina — a 10-hour window is a downtown visit, not a city tour.
